task.description: Hard gate REQ-073's Step 2a implementation (five real user-CRUD route handlers, first network-reachable identity CRUD in Letflow) against security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8.
acceptance_criteria: Every applicable invariant (INV-1, INV-2, INV-4, INV-5, INV-6, INV-7, INV-8) checked against the actual diff with its own How-to-verify procedure
AC4's structural authorization-before-any-Repo-call guarantee traced by hand across all five handlers
INV-2 response allowlist confirmed hand-built, exactly 8 keys, no Jason.Encoder/@derive leak path
Cursor-pagination mint-time deviation independently checked against Pagination.decode_cursor/4's actual contract for a new security defect, not just for correctness

result.summary:
Scope test: this diff is squarely in scope -- new tenant-scoped API routes (lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex), new response-shaping code for a tenant-scoped entity (user_map/1), and a lookup-by-ID handler (GET/PATCH/status /users/:id). Reviewed against INV-1..INV-8 individually.

INV-1 (tenant isolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. Every Letflow.Identity function (create_user/2, list_users/2, get_user/2, update_user_profile/3, update_user_status/3) takes opts :: [prefix: String.t()] with Keyword.fetch!(opts, :prefix) (raises if absent, never defaults to public) and threads :prefix into every Repo.insert/Repo.all/Repo.get/Repo.update call -- verified by reading lib/letflow/identity.ex lines 192-298 directly, no exceptions. opts is derived exclusively from Letflow.Api.Context.scoped_repo_opts(conn) in the router's with_authorized_scope/4 preamble (identity.ex:93-119) -- no handler accepts or constructs a schema name itself. Confirmed via grep: no other lib/letflow/plugs/*.ex or api/context.ex file changed beyond the review scope (git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/plugs/ lib/letflow/api/context.ex is empty). No tenant_id column exists on users post-Decision-0006-D2 so (c) of the verification procedure is N/A by design, confirmed against lib/letflow/identity/user.ex's schema (no tenant_id field) and its moduledoc explaining the 0006 D2 drop. Cross-tenant-404 test (identity_test.exs:186-201) and tenant-isolation list test (identity_test.exs:269-285) read directly: both use TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 (real provisioned Postgres schemas, not simulated) and insert_user!/2 (real Repo.insert! against tenant.schema_name) -- genuine, not simulated.

INV-2 (server-side field allowlist) -- APPLIES (S4 route now exists), PASS. user_map/1 (identity.ex router lines 317-333) is a hand-built map literal with exactly 8 keys (id, username, display_name, email, status, auth_source, inserted_at, updated_at) built from named struct field reads, never derived. Grepped the whole diff for Jason.Encoder/@derive on Letflow.Identity.User -- zero hits; the only two @derive{Jason.Encoder} references in the codebase are on Letflow.Api.Pagination.Page (items/next_cursor/count only, pre-existing REQ-067 code, not touched by this diff) and unrelated modules -- no path exists for password_hash/external_id/external_realm to reach a JSON response.

INV-4 (secrets by reference) -- APPLIES, PASS. No new secret-resolving code in this diff; grep for System.get_env/hardcoded-secret patterns in the touched files returns nothing relevant.

INV-5 (cross-tenant 404 indistinguishability) -- APPLIES (first lookup-by-ID endpoint), PASS. handle_get/3, handle_patch/3, handle_status_update/3 all route through Identity.get_user/2, which does a single Repo.get(User, id, prefix: prefix) and returns {:error, :not_found} uniformly whether the id belongs to another tenant's schema (never visible to this prefix at all) or doesn't exist anywhere -- there is structurally no code path that can distinguish the two, since a cross-tenant row isn't even queryable under this prefix. Router's not_found branch calls Response.not_found(conn) identically in both cases. Test at identity_test.exs:186-201 verifies byte-identical status and resp_body between a real cross-tenant probe and a genuinely-absent-id probe.

INV-6 (new data-access path proves its scoping) -- this handoff itself satisfies it.

INV-7 (no raw SQL) -- APPLIES, PASS. grep for Repo.query across lib/letflow/identity.ex and lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex: zero hits. All queries go through Ecto.Query (import Ecto.Query, from/2, ilike/2 with pinned ^ params).

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes) -- APPLIES, PASS. Grepped for bare `{:ok, _} = `/`{:error, _} = ` patterns in both files: the two hits in identity.ex (lines 200, 444) are inside case clauses already matching on Repo.insert/2's own two-tuple return shape, not unconstrained; the three hits in routers/identity.ex (lines 98, 115, 214) are all inside a case already branching on {:error, _} separately, so each bare-looking match is reached only after the alternative shape was already excluded. The one router-level bare match on Identity.list_users/2's result (`{:ok, %{...}} = Identity.list_users(...)`, handle_list/1) is safe because list_users/2's own @spec and implementation (identity.ex:223-241) only ever return {:ok, _} -- never {:error, _} -- so this is the 'immediately after a value the same function already validated' exception the invariant's own text names, not an unhandled failure path.

Cursor-pagination mint-time deviation (flagged by ELIXIR-DEV) -- independently verified against Letflow.Api.Pagination.decode_cursor/4's actual contract (lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex:168-201): decode_cursor checks (1) base64url decode, (2) check_prefix/2 -- a literal string-prefix match on the endpoint tag ("U:"), completely independent of which payload field holds the timestamp, (3) extract_expiry_timestamp/2 at a caller-supplied byte offset, checked for staleness against wall-clock now. The router calls decode_cursor(raw, "U:", byte_size("U:")) -- offset 2, which lands on the payload's first field after the prefix. ELIXIR-DEV placed System.system_time(:microsecond) (mint time) in that exact first field and moved the real sort key (inserted_at_us) and tiebreaker (id) to the second/third fields, parsed separately by Letflow.Identity's own decode_users_cursor/1 (not by Pagination's generic helpers). This does not touch or weaken cross-endpoint replay prevention: that property is entirely carried by check_prefix/2's literal string match, which is untouched by which field holds the timestamp. It also does not weaken INV-1/INV-5's cursor-side guarantee, which is structural (Cursor.t() has only an `inner :: binary()` field, no tenant/schema slot, per pagination.ex's own moduledoc) and unaffected by field-slot semantics. Using mint-time is in fact the functionally correct interpretation of 'expiry' (bounding how long an issued cursor stays valid) -- using row-time as the design literally suggested would have made any cursor built from a >24h-old row appear pre-expired at issuance, which is a correctness bug, not a security property this project relies on. Verdict: the deviation is a bug fix, introduces no new security issue, and does not conflict with REQ-067's design intent for Pagination.

Password_hash sentinel ("__NO_PASSWORD_SET__") -- verified no login/authentication code path exists yet anywhere in lib/ that reads or compares User.password_hash against a caller-supplied credential (grepped all 7 hits of "password_hash" across the repo: 2 are code -- user.ex's schema/changeset and identity.ex's design-doc references -- both are write-only; the rest are design docs). No coincidental-match risk exists today because there is no comparison call site at all.

Permission-denial tests (AC4) read directly: POST test asserts Repo.aggregate(User, :count, prefix: ...) unchanged before/after the 403; PATCH and status-update tests assert Repo.get!(User, id, prefix: ...) returns a byte-identical struct before/after -- genuine full-row/row-count checks, not a second status-code check.

Scope (git diff main...HEAD --stat): only the expected file set changed (identity.ex router+context module, user.ex schema, one additive authorization.ex clause, new test file, plus handoff/status bookkeeping). Confirmed no touch to lib/letflow/plugs/*.ex or lib/letflow/api/context.ex beyond the single named endpoint_policy_key/2 clause.

All checked invariants PASS. No FAIL. Status: PASS.
